To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the access pattern of data stored on a network storage system is multi-dimensional and can be used to optimize storage system designs and performance.

(1) data access patterns are not uniform, (2) data access patterns vary significantly across different dimensions (e.g., users and applications), and (3) the data access patterns are stable over time.

(i) the majority of data accesses are to a small subset of files, (ii) data accesses are highly skewed across users, applications, files, and directories, and (iii) the data access patterns exhibit a strong locality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and optimization of enterprise storage systems via the analysis of multi-dimensional data access patterns.
developing a comprehensive methodology to obtain design insights for future storage systems.
the design implications of storage systems via a multi-dimensional trace analysis method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology provides an objective and multi-dimensional view on the data access patterns of enterprise network storage systems that enables the derivation of design optimizations.
our method is a very useful tool for storage system designers, administrators, and researchers to understand the data access behavior of their systems.

we provide a new methodology for extracting data access patterns from large-scale traces, and we demonstrate the effectiveness of our methodology by applying it to two large-scale traces and extracting design insights that lead to simple, yet effective design optimizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present an innovative, objective, statistical approach that enables the extraction of data access patterns from storage system traces and provides design insights and optimizations for network storage systems.
our method provides a new approach for storage systems design and analysis, and that our design optimizations provide significant improvements in performance and capacity.
we have developed an objective, multi-level methodology for extracting data access patterns and design implications from storage traces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multi-dimensional analysis method is an effective and practical tool for extracting design implications from real-world traces.
the proposed multi-dimensional trace analysis method can be used by system designers to derive simple, yet effective design optimizations that improve storage systems performance and capacity.
the multi-dimensional trace analysis method is an effective way of gaining insights that can be used to improve storage system design.
